{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   --job-name="SpTrSv_Final"
#   --output="SpTrSv_Final_%j.out"
#   --error="SpTrSv_Final_%j.error"
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks-per-node=64
#   --export=ALL
#   -t 6:00:00

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 64 \
  --time=6h \
  bash -lc '

# Approximate Slurm %j with Flux job id.
exec >"SpTrSv_Final_${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>"SpTrSv_Final_${FLUX_JOB_ID}.error"

# NOTE: Slurm --job-name=SpTrSv_Final is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

# Slurm --export=ALL: environment is typically inherited by the shell here.

source init_var.sh
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=64
export MKL_NUM_THREADS=64

SOURCE_DIR=$(pwd)
echo "Start SpTrSv Final"
cd "${SOURCE_DIR}/build/example"
rm -rf SpTrSv_Final_20.csv

for sparse_mat in matrix/*.mtx; do
    echo "Processing ${sparse_mat}"
    ./SpTrSv_Final "${sparse_mat}"
done
'
"
}
